name: Wool felt
summary: A non-woven sheet of wool fibres locked together by moisture, heat and agitation. In the Reserve it is the mat on which a Degas pastel lies in each south plan chest; in the Salon it lines the floor of the 1874 case under the catalogue and Le Charivari.

whyAnAccent.text: The material-language board groups the cloths with the timber: 'D · The oak, and what it carries: timber, leather, silk, felt'. Each cloth is declared an accent of the oak family (D-014); the Architect may overturn this reading.
whyAnAccent.source: MuseeVision/Journal/Decisions.md, D-014 (Matter: every substance carries its family; an accent names its core family); plan/canvas/MaterialsOther.dc.html, section 'D · The oak, and what it carries'

formation.how: Layers of wool are wetted with hot water and repeatedly agitated and compressed: heat, moisture and motion open the scales on each fibre, and agitation makes them latch onto one another, so the fibres felt into one sheet, which fulling then densifies.

wetFelting.text: Hot water is applied to layers of animal hairs, while repeated agitation and compression causes the fibres to hook together; the scales open with heat, motion and moisture and latch on agitation; the felt may be finished by fulling.

optics.note: A dense, matt, fibrous surface: diffuse, with a faint grazing sheen from loose fibre ends (asperity scattering, as velvet's but weaker).

asperityScattering.text: Sparse scatterers such as hairs add a grazing surface lobe.
asperityScattering.source: Koenderink, J.J. & Pont, S.C. (2003) The secret of velvety skin. Machine Vision and Applications 14, 260-268, https://doi.org/10.1007/s00138-002-0089-7 (abstract read)

reserveFelt.source: plan/canvas/MaterialsOther.dc.html, section 'D · The oak, and what it carries' ('Wool felt · M_Felt #4E5A4C · matt 0.95')
reserveFelt.conditions: the Reserve's plan-chest mats: a green-grey, matt
reserveFelt.derivation: the design's sRGB hex decoded with the sRGB transfer function; a design colour, not a measurement

physical.note: Density and thickness of the chosen felt are unverified.

acoustic.note: Small mats and linings inside chests and a case: not a room surface. No absorption is recorded.

stock.note: Cut from sheet; thickness and density were not read (see unverified).

sulfur.text: Wool is a pollutant source for metals: a nineteenth-century coin balance's brass cups are blackened in lines wherever wool threads touched them.
sulfur.source: Tétreault, J. (2021) Agent of deterioration: pollutants. Canadian Conservation Institute, 2021-02-17, https://www.canada.ca/en/conservation-institute/services/agents-deterioration/pollutants.html (Figure 10)

conservation.rule: A felt near silver, brass or lead must be tested before use (an accelerated corrosion test); the 1874 case holds paper only and the pastels lie on felt in their chests, so the felt stays, tested. Wool is also food for moth and beetle larvae.

uses.where: the Reserve: the felt mat under a Degas pastel on each south plan chest

evidence.shows: A wool felt at 0.5 m: the nap and its fine mottle.
